beginner.stem: How many protons does a Sodium atom have? (That number is also its place on the table.)
beginner.explanation: Sodium is element 11. A neutral atom has 11 protons and 11 electrons.

beginner.explanation: The catalog writes Sodium as Na.

beginner.stem: Which element has the symbol Na?
beginner.explanation: Na is Sodium, atomic number 11.

beginner.stem: Which column of the table holds Sodium? (Columns are called groups.)

beginner.stem: Which block of the table contains Sodium? (Blocks are s, p, d, or f.)

beginner.stem: What boiling point does this catalog list for Sodium?

beginner.stem: Which of these is a listed use of Sodium?
beginner.explanation: Table salt is sodium chloride. The sodium in it has already reacted and is part of a calm crystal, not the soft metal.

beginner.stem: Which of these is a listed use of Sodium?
beginner.explanation: Older yellow street lamps were sodium vapor. In the body, sodium ions help nerve cells send signals.

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Sodium in this catalog?
beginner.explanation: Humphry Davy had just pulled a metal from potash when he turned the same current on melted caustic soda. Another silvery substance was about to appear.

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Sodium in this catalog?

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Sodium in this catalog?

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Sodium in this catalog?

beginner.stem: What color name does the catalog give the 388.18 nm line of Sodium?
beginner.explanation: That Sodium line is labelled violet.

beginner.explanation: Hydrogen shares group 1 with Sodium.
